questions.q: What is the key difference between a Novice-level speaker and an Intermediate-level speaker of a language?
options: Novice speakers use more vocabulary words
Intermediate speakers can create original sentences and connect them into a paragraph, not just recycle memorized phrases
There is no real difference, only test scores differ
questions.explanation: The shift from Novice to Intermediate is about generating original, connected language, not just knowing more words.

questions.q: According to Washington law (RCW 28A.300.575), what proficiency level does the Seal of Biliteracy require in a world language?
questions.explanation: The Seal of Biliteracy law sets the world-language bar at Intermediate Mid.

questions.q: Under WA's competency-based credit crosswalk (RCW 28A.230.090), how many credits does Intermediate Mid or higher proficiency earn?
questions.explanation: Intermediate Mid or higher earns 4 credits, the same level the Seal requires.

questions.q: What is WA's minimum graduation requirement in this same credit system, and which level does it represent?
questions.explanation: Graduation only requires Novice High (2 credits) — two levels below the Seal's Intermediate Mid threshold.

questions.q: What is a 'can-do statement,' the tool you used this week for your baseline self-assessment?
options: A grammar rule you must memorize
A description of what a speaker can actually do at a given proficiency level
A list of vocabulary words for a unit
A grade on a Spanish test
questions.explanation: Can-do statements describe real-world tasks a speaker can perform at each proficiency level, not knowledge or grades.

questions.q: What does la meta a largo plazo, the phrase behind today's goal-statement writing task, mean?
questions.explanation: La meta a largo plazo means 'the long-term goal' — the specific, dated proficiency target the student wrote today.
